cycle.title: Four moves: convert, cite, stack, deliver.
cycle.lede: This is not a chat with a PDF attached. It is the whole loop — from the raw file nobody can search to the deliverable you can actually defend.

convert.title: From raw file to blocks you can search.
convert.body: Drop in a PDF, a scan or a table and Doctiling rebuilds it: page geometry so reading order survives, tables reassembled as tables, images pushed through OCR in the background, and cuts made at section boundaries — not every 8,000 characters. What comes out is an editable document, not an opaque attachment.

bullets.p1: PDF tables rebuilt from geometry, not flattened into prose
bullets.p2: Images and scans OCR'd on a durable queue — keep working while it runs
bullets.p3: Blocks cut at headings, so one block is one idea

convert.scenario: A firm loads a 60-page scanned contract their own search engine could not even open.
convert.outcome: It comes out as a document with readable blocks and tables — and from that moment it is citable material.

cite.title: The block is the unit of the answer.
cite.body: Every block is embedded in 768 dimensions and indexed on its own. When you ask, the agent retrieves blocks — not whole documents — and answers with a citation to the exact one. If the answer is not in your sources, it says so.

bullets.p1: Block-level citations: one click lands you on the source paragraph
bullets.p2: Meaning-based search across the whole knowledge base
bullets.p3: Multi-turn chat that keeps the document in focus

cite.scenario: “Which contracts renew this quarter, and at what penalty?” — across forty agreements at once.
cite.outcome: Back comes a table where every row links to the clause it came from: verifying takes a click, not an afternoon.

stack.title: Twelve analysis lenses, stacked beside the document.
stack.body: Mirror view splits the screen: your document on one side, the analyses on the other. Summary, entities, contradictions, comparison table, mind map, questions, critique — plus five lenses for table documents. Each one runs on the indexed content and stacks without erasing the last.

bullets.p1: Twelve one-click lenses — no prompt writing
bullets.p2: Analyze, synthesize and dialogue modes; fast, balanced or deep tier
bullets.p3: Diagrams and mind maps rendered inside the document

stack.scenario: A consultancy uploads three market reports and asks where they contradict each other before the client call.
stack.outcome: The mirror shows every disagreement next to the clashing paragraphs — ready to take into the deck.

deliver.title: The analysis becomes your document — or an endpoint.
deliver.body: Save any analysis as a variant: an editable document that keeps its trail back to the sources, ready to keep working on and to share with roles. Or expose the knowledge base as an MCP endpoint with a scoped, revocable token, so it answers from the tools your team already works in.

bullets.p1: Editable variants with the trail to the source intact
bullets.p2: Owner, admin, collaborator and reader roles — with per-user private analyses
bullets.p3: Read-only MCP endpoint, scoped per token, revocable

deliver.scenario: A research group shares its literature base and queries it from their own MCP-compatible client.
deliver.outcome: One indexed corpus, many ways to work — and private analyses still belong to whoever made them.

docTypes.title: A document is not always text. Your base holds all three shapes.
docTypes.lede: Your team's knowledge doesn't fit one format: there is prose, there are rows, and there are relationships. Doctiling stores all three in the same knowledge base, indexes them the same way, and the agent cites any of them.

text.title: Text document

bullets.p1: Blocks cut at headings, not every 8,000 characters
bullets.p2: Background OCR for images and scanned pages

table.title: Table document
table.body: Upload a table or connect a read-only SQL engine. The agent queries the rows, aggregates and compares — and the table is indexed as readable rows, not raw JSON, so semantic search finds it too.

graph.title: Graph document

faq.title: Everything you'd ask before signing in.

what.a: A knowledge management system. Your information lives in knowledge bases you govern — one per client, team or case — with documents, tables and graphs, its own system prompt, its own tools and its own permissions. Your experts curate that content and AI agents analyse it, compare it and turn it into tables, charts, diagrams and code, always citing where each claim came from. The base is shared with your team, published or connected over MCP to the tools you already use.

dms.q: Is it a document manager or a vector search engine?
dms.a: Neither, although it does what both do. It stores your sources with permissions and indexes them by meaning, but that is where its work starts: structuring them into documents, tables and graphs, letting your experts curate them — edit, validate, retire what is stale — and having AI agents analyse them with citations. What you get is not a file found, but verified knowledge you can reuse, share and query from other tools.

grounded.q: How is this different from a generic AI chat?
grounded.a: Generic chats answer from memory and sometimes invent. Doctiling indexes every block of your documents and retrieves the relevant passages before answering, so every claim ships with a citation back to your own content. If it's not in your sources, the agent says so instead of guessing.

rag.q: Does this replace the RAG project we were going to build in-house?
rag.a: For most cases, yes. Chunking, embedding, the vector index and citation are already built and tested; you need no pipeline of your own and nobody to maintain it. What stays in your hands is what actually decides the outcome: which sources enter each base, who has access, which tools the agent may call and which systems query it. If your case demands full control of the stack, the self-hosted build runs the same product on your infrastructure.

privacy.a: Only you and the people you explicitly invite, under roles (owner, admin, collaborator, reader). On the Free plan your data is logically isolated per user; Gold moves you to your own dedicated database, and Platinum adds dedicated infrastructure on top.

free.q: How do I get free access?
free.a: Free access is sponsored and invitation-only. Request a demo with your email; once we approve it you can sign in and use the full studio — knowledge bases, document editor, AI agent with citations, mirror view, custom tools — with a sponsored AI budget and a quota of 25 AI calls per day. No credit card, no trial clock. Upgrade only if you need isolation or higher volume.

mcp.q: What is MCP and why should I care?
mcp.a: Model Context Protocol is an open standard that lets external AI tools read from a data source. With Doctiling you can expose a knowledge base through a scoped, revocable, read-only token, so the desktop AI tools your team already uses can query your documents as a source of truth.

langs.a: Yes — the whole studio is bilingual (Spanish and English) and you can switch at any moment. The agent reads and answers in the language of your documents and your questions.

differentiator.title: A process no longer needs a system. It needs a knowledge base and an agent.
differentiator.lede: Today every internal process (leave, certificates, appointments, orders) means building a system: data model, screens, permissions, integrations and maintenance. Or it lives in email and spreadsheets. Doctiling changes the starting point: the information is already organised in knowledge bases with their own access hierarchy. The tenant is the agentic semantic layer that queries and manages them. A small agent, connected to the right base, is the process.

hero.title: An AI studio that speaks your profession's language.
hero.lede: Doctiling isn't a generic chat. It's a space where your own documents answer — with the exact citation, not a guess. We tune it for the real work of each field: contracts, patient records, financial statements, papers, data rooms. Here's what changes when your field stops pasting PDFs into a chat and starts asking its sources.

legal.title: Legal teams
legal.tagline: From the matter file to the brief, without losing the exact clause.
legal.problem: Reviewing contracts and building a case theory means re-reading hundreds of pages and praying you don't miss the clause that changes everything. Generic AI chats summarize well but invent citations — and a fabricated citation in a filing is a professional liability.
legal.solution: Upload the full matter file to a knowledge base. Ask in plain language and the agent answers citing the document and the exact page. Generate briefs, timelines and clause-comparison tables, every statement traceable to its source.
legal.edge: Answers you can defend to a client or a judge. On the Gold plan your matters live in a dedicated database — never mixed with another firm's. White-label so you deliver under your own brand.

capabilities.c1: Contract review with clause extraction and comparison.
capabilities.c2: Case briefs and case-law summaries with verbatim citations.

health.title: Healthcare
health.tagline: Patient history, guidelines and literature in one place — cited.
health.problem: Patient information lives scattered across notes, labs and clinical guidelines. Finding a history or cross-checking a finding against the literature eats the time that should go to care. And an assistant that invents a dose is unacceptable.
health.solution: Bring patient history, guidelines and papers into a knowledge base. The agent suggests differentials, summarizes follow-ups and answers clinical questions always citing the source. If something isn't in your documents, it says so — it doesn't invent it.
health.edge: End-to-end clinical traceability: never a fabricated dose or finding. Your data is isolated per user, and paid plans move it to dedicated infrastructure for sensitive environments.

capabilities.c1: Differentials grounded in guidelines and literature.
capabilities.c2: Progress notes and patient follow-up summaries with citations.

chat.a: Visit recorded, next one in 4 weeks. Target < 140/90 over 65 without frailty; individualise if frail. If it were not in your sources, I would say so.

finance.title: Finance
finance.tagline: Every figure points to the statement it came from.
finance.problem: Analyzing reports, computing ratios and tracking a portfolio means jumping between endless PDFs and spreadsheets. An untraced number is a number you can't audit — or defend to an investment committee.
finance.solution: Upload filings, statements and reports to a knowledge base. Ask for ratio analysis, executive summaries and period-over-period comparisons; every figure links to the exact statement it came from. Stack analyses beside the document in mirror view.
finance.edge: Audit-ready analysis from minute one: no fabricated numbers, everything traceable. Per-tenant data isolation for sensitive market information.

accounting.title: Accounting
accounting.tagline: Close stops being a hunt for receipts.
accounting.problem: Classifying transactions, reconciling accounts and tracing an entry in the general ledger is manual, error-prone work. When close or audit arrives, finding the support for each movement takes hours.
accounting.solution: Load ledgers, receipts and policies into a knowledge base. Classify transactions, reconcile and query the ledger by asking in plain language. Every answer links back to the original entry.
accounting.edge: Full audit traceability: every figure traces to its support. Fewer close hours, less risk of findings.

research.title: Research & grad school
research.tagline: From a stack of papers to a literature review with real citations.
research.problem: A literature review is weeks of reading, annotating and cross-referencing. AI chats speed it up but fabricate references that don't exist — poison for a thesis or a paper.
research.solution: Upload your paper corpus to a knowledge base. Synthesize across sources, surface contradictions, extract methods and results, and draft with verifiable citations to your own documents. A bilingual studio for writing in English or Spanish.
research.edge: Verifiable citations, never invented references. Bilingual EN · ES so you can publish in either language. Save each synthesis as a variant and compare approaches without losing the trail.

capabilities.c1: Literature review with synthesis across multiple sources.
capabilities.c2: Contradiction and gap detection in the state of the art.
capabilities.c3: Extraction of methods, data and results with citations.

chat.u: Synthesise the papers on the effect in older adults and create the review document.
chat.a: 12 relevant papers. Ortega 2023 reports a significant effect; Lin & Park 2022 do not find it over 70. The review includes the methods table and the contradictions, every cell linked to its block.

consulting.title: Consulting
consulting.tagline: Data rooms and interviews turned into grounded deliverables.
consulting.problem: A project starts with hundreds of client documents, transcripts and data rooms. Turning all of that into a clear, defensible deliverable is where billable time goes — and the client wants to see the trail, not a black box.
consulting.solution: Centralize the data room in a knowledge base. Mirror view stacks summaries, entity tables, mind maps and correlations beside the document. Save each finding as a variant and expose the knowledge base to your team chat over MCP.
consulting.edge: Deliverables traceable to the source document: the client sees where each conclusion comes from. Expose the knowledge base to the tools your team already uses — Doctiling is the cited memory layer behind your workflow.
